title: Why Planes Leave White Lines in the Sky
lines: Why do planes leave white lines in the sky?
It's not smoke. It's actually a cloud made of ice.
Burning jet fuel makes hot exhaust full of water vapor.
But up at cruising height, the air can be colder than minus forty degrees.
So the water vapor freezes into tiny ice crystals almost instantly.
Billions of them form a long, thin cloud behind the plane.
If the air is dry, the line disappears fast. If it's humid, it can last for hours.
They're called contrails, short for condensation trails. Follow for more!
caption:
Those white lines behind planes are clouds ✈️❄️ Jet exhaust is full of water vapor, and at ~10 km the air is below −40 °C, so it freezes into ice crystals. Dry air = they vanish fast. Humid air = they can last for hours.
